newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed says Fermi nuke shut 4 more wks.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed says Fermi nuke shut 4 more wks.

text.p: Detroit Edison said Tuesday that its Fermi 2 nuclear power plant will remain shut for at least four more weeks while the company rebuilds a main generator in the non-nuclear part of the plant.
The unit has been disconnected from the power grid since September 27, when it was shut for scheduled maintenance.
A series of technical problems at the facility have prevented the company from bringing the unit back into service following completion of the maintenance work.
"(Fermi) will be shut down for a least four weeks," spokeswoman Mary Kay Bean said, adding "there may be some electrical or heat damage to some of the generator components."
The unit was producing electricity but was not synchronized to the electricity grid on Friday when the generator problem caused the reactor to trip, Bean said.
The plant, in Newport, Mich., has a rated capacity of 1,116 megawatts (MW) but had been operating previous to the maintenance shutdown at a maximum of 1,075 MW due to some technical problems.
Fermi 2 makes up about 15 percent of Detroit Edison's power generation capacity. The company supplies about two million southeast Michigan customers with electricity.
Detroit Edison may purchase some power on the open market to replace generation lost by the extended Fermi outage, Bean said.
"We had been buying some power because it was economic, and we may be in that situation again depending on the economics," the spokeswoman said.
